COMPUTER STUDIES OCTOBER — MOCK EXAM #9
====

GRADE: Grade 11
SUBJECT: COMPUTER STUDIES OCTOBER
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours
TOTAL MARKS: 80
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When learning Network Security, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Skip safety briefings for Network Security.
   B. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Network Security.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Network Security.
   D. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Network Security.

2. When learning Binary Arithmetic Operations, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Binary Arithmetic Operations.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Binary Arithmetic Operations.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Binary Arithmetic Operations.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Binary Arithmetic Operations.

3. When learning Logic Gates, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Logic Gates.
   B. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Logic Gates.
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Logic Gates.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Logic Gates.

4. When learning Relational Database Fundamentals, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Skip safety briefings for Relational Database Fundamentals.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Relational Database Fundamentals.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Relational Database Fundamentals.
   D. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Relational Database Fundamentals.

5. When learning Object Oriented Programming Concepts, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Object Oriented Programming Concepts.
   B. Skip safety briefings for Object Oriented Programming Concepts.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Object Oriented Programming Concepts.
   D. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Object Oriented Programming Concepts.

6. When learning Structured Query Language, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Structured Query Language.
   B. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Structured Query Language.
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Structured Query Language.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Structured Query Language.

7. A computer’s main brain for processing is the: (1 mark)
   A. CPU
   B. Monitor
   C. Keyboard
   D. Speaker

8. When learning Data Representation, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Data Representation.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Data Representation.
   C. Skip safety briefings for Data Representation.
   D. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Data Representation.

9. Electricity safety rule: (1 mark)
   A. Overload every socket
   B. Insert metal objects into sockets for fun
   C. Never touch live wires with wet hands
   D. Ignore burnt cables

10. ICT stands for: (1 mark)
   A. Information and Communication Technology
   B. Internal Cooking Timer
   C. International Cricket Team
   D. Input Cable Tester

11. When learning Web Development Fundamentals, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Web Development Fundamentals.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Web Development Fundamentals.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Web Development Fundamentals.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Web Development Fundamentals.

12. Before using a sharp tool in a workshop, you should: (1 mark)
   A. Run with the tool
   B. Remove all guards
   C. Wear safety gear and follow instructions
   D. Work alone with eyes closed

13. When learning Logic Circuits, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Logic Circuits.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Logic Circuits.
   C. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Logic Circuits.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Logic Circuits.

14. When learning Computer Network Standards and Protocols, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Computer Network Standards and Protocols.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Computer Network Standards and Protocols.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Computer Network Standards and Protocols.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Computer Network Standards and Protocols.

15. When learning Object Oriented Programming Implementation, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Object Oriented Programming Implementation.
   B. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Object Oriented Programming Implementation.
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Object Oriented Programming Implementation.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Object Oriented Programming Implementation.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. In three clear sentences, explain Web Development Fundamentals and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

17. In three clear sentences, explain Data Representation and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Binary Arithmetic Operations and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Logic Gates and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

20. In three clear sentences, explain Logic Circuits and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

21. In three clear sentences, explain Computer Network Standards and Protocols and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

22. In three clear sentences, explain Network Security and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

23. In three clear sentences, explain Object Oriented Programming Concepts and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
